name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.24.0 (released 2026-06-04, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.24.0) is the latest release, introducing an opt-in in-memory ACL cache (`auth-access-cache`) to reduce database load on high-volume self-hosted servers, along with a security fix for case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite (LIKE was matching 'secret' and 'SECRET' interchangeably). Recent versions (v2.20.0–v2.23.0) added S3-compatible attachment storage, email recipient verification (`smtp-sender-verify`), per-visitor topic creation rate limits, and several security fixes including an SSRF fix in web push endpoint handling (GHSA-w9hq-5jg7-q4j7) and a same-origin script execution fix in the publish dialog (GHSA-j8hr-p342-xrmh). The project is actively maintained with frequent releases across 2025–2026.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (based on the ntfy project; not explicitly stated in changelog but documented in the repository)
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2025–2026 with regular bug fixes and features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — ACL-based topic authorization with both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends, including an in-memory ACL cache as of v2.24.0
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted instance

breaking_excerpts: v2.20.0: ntfy will take full control over the attachment-cache-dir or S3 bucket — files matching the message ID format (^[A-Za-z0-9]{12}$) with no database entries will be deleted. Do not reuse the attachment directory for other purposes.
v2.24.0 (security): Fix case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite — a rule for 'secret' no longer matches requests for 'SECRET'; behavior change for existing SQLite-based ACL configurations.
v2.21.0: smtp-sender-verify flag added requiring email address verification before sending notifications; ntfy.sh enforces this going forward due to AWS SES suspension.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing but is a proprietary cloud service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting.

alternatives.name: ntopng / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager excels at routing and deduplicating alerts in monitoring pipelines but is purpose-built for metrics alerting rather than general-purpose push notifications.
